questions.question: What is the solution to the equation $3x^2+5x-1=0$?
Express $4x\sqrt{11}$ in the form of $\sqrt a$.
Which of the Venn diagrams best represents $A\cap\overline B$?
questions.answer: $A\cap\overline B$ is the set of elements in $A$ that are not in $B$: the part of circle $A$ outside circle $B$ (A). Diagram B is $A\cap B$, C is $\overline B$ (everything outside $B$) and D is $B\cap\overline A$.

questions.question: What is the domain of $f(x)=\log_{10}\big[(x-3)(x-5)\big]$?
questions.answer: The logarithm requires $(x-3)(x-5)>0$. The parabola $y=(x-3)(x-5)$ is positive outside its roots, so $x<3$ or $x>5$ (D).

questions.question: Which of the following diagrams best represents a standardised normally distributed dataset with the interquartile range shaded?
questions.answer: The interquartile range contains the middle $50\%$ of the data. For a standard normal distribution this is about $-0.67<z<0.67$, i.e. a region narrower than $\pm1$ standard deviation (which would contain about $68\%$). Only diagram A shades such a narrow, symmetric region (A).

questions.question: The area enclosed by the function $y=x(x-1)(2-x)$ and the $x$-axis can be described as:
questions.answer: The curve crosses the $x$-axis at $x=0,1,2$. For $0<x<1$: $x>0$, $x-1<0$, $2-x>0$, so $y<0$ (below the axis). For $1<x<2$ all three factors are positive, so $y>0$. The area is the positive value of each part: $-\int_0^1y\,dx+\int_1^2y\,dx$ (D).

questions.question: The displacement of a car from a reference point along a straight road that runs east–west is $x$ kilometres. The car is initially $100$ metres east of the reference point. The graph below shows the displacement of the car at time $t$ seconds. When the car is at point $P$, which statement reflects its motion?
questions.answer: At $P$ the displacement is decreasing (the gradient is negative), so the velocity is negative: the car is moving west (towards the reference point and beyond). The graph is concave down at $P$, so the acceleration is negative as well; velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the speed is increasing (B).
options: The car is moving east, and its speed is increasing.
The car is moving west, and its speed is increasing.
The car is moving east, and its speed is decreasing.
The car is moving west, and its speed is decreasing.

questions.question: Which of the following functions has a period of $\dfrac\pi2$ and is increasing in the domain $\left(\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac\pi2\right)$?
questions.answer: $\sin|x|$ and $\cos|x|$ have period $2\pi$, so A and C are out. $|\sin2x|$ and $|\cos2x|$ both have period $\dfrac\pi2$. For $\dfrac\pi4<x<\dfrac\pi2$, $\pi/2<2x<\pi$: $\sin2x$ falls from $1$ to $0$ (so $|\sin2x|$ is decreasing), while $\cos2x$ goes from $0$ to $-1$ so $|\cos2x|$ rises from $0$ to $1$ (increasing) (D).

questions.question: Find an expression, in simplest form, for the general term of the arithmetic series $257+246+235+\cdots$
Find the $125$th term of the series $257+246+235+\cdots$

A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability distribution table below.

| $X=x$ | 5 | 10 | 15 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $P(x)$ | 0.1 | 0.25 | $n$ | 0.35 |

Find the value of $n$.
questions.answer: The probabilities sum to $1$: $0.1+0.25+n+0.35=1\Rightarrow n=0.3$.

questions.question: (Distribution: $P(5)=0.1$, $P(10)=0.25$, $P(15)=0.3$, $P(20)=0.35$.) Find the expected value $E(X)$.

The shaded segment shown is formed by an arc $BC$ of a circle with radius $1.6$ m. The arc subtends an angle of $\dfrac{4\pi}9$ radians at its centre, $A$. Find the area of the shaded segment, correct to $3$ significant figures.
questions.answer:
Segment area = sector area $-$ triangle area:
$$A=\tfrac12r^2\theta-\tfrac12r^2\sin\theta=\tfrac12(1.6)^2\left(\frac{4\pi}9-\sin\frac{4\pi}9\right)=1.28(1.3963-0.9848)\approx0.527\ \text{m}^2$$

questions.question: Given $\log_52=a$ and $\log_53=b$, express $\log_5\left(\dfrac{12}{\sqrt2}\right)$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.
questions.answer:
$\dfrac{12}{\sqrt2}=6\sqrt2=2\cdot3\cdot2^{1/2}=2^{3/2}\cdot3$, so
$$\log_5\left(2^{3/2}\cdot3\right)=\tfrac32\log_52+\log_53=\tfrac32a+b$$

questions.question: Differentiate $y=(3x^2-7)^6$ with respect to $x$.
Differentiate $y=\dfrac{2x-1}{x+8}$ with respect to $x$.
Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y=x^3+\ln x+5$ at the point $(1,6)$.
questions.answer: $y'=3x^2+\dfrac1x$, so at $x=1$ the gradient is $m=3+1=4$. Tangent: $y-6=4(x-1)\Rightarrow y=4x+2$.

questions.question: If $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt5}5$, $0<x<\dfrac\pi2$, find the value of $\sin^4x-\cos^4x$.
questions.answer:
$\sin^4x-\cos^4x=(\sin^2x-\cos^2x)(\sin^2x+\cos^2x)=\sin^2x-\cos^2x=2\sin^2x-1$.
With $\sin^2x=\dfrac15$: $2\left(\dfrac15\right)-1=-\dfrac35$.

questions.question: Solve for $x$ where $0\le x\le2\pi$: $\operatorname{cosec}\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)=\sqrt2$.
questions.answer:
$\sin\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}$, and $\dfrac\pi3\le x+\dfrac\pi3\le\dfrac{7\pi}3$. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so
$$x+\frac\pi3=\frac\pi4\ (\text{rejected, below }\tfrac\pi3),\ \frac{3\pi}4,\ \frac{9\pi}4,\ \frac{11\pi}4\ (\text{rejected, above }\tfrac{7\pi}3).$$
$$x=\frac{3\pi}4-\frac\pi3=\frac{5\pi}{12}\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{9\pi}4-\frac\pi3=\frac{23\pi}{12}$$

questions.question: Show that $\sec^2A\equiv\dfrac{\operatorname{cosec}A}{\operatorname{cosec}A-\sin A}$.
questions.answer:
Start with the right-hand side and multiply the numerator and denominator by $\sin A$:
$$\text{RHS}=\frac{\operatorname{cosec}A}{\operatorname{cosec}A-\sin A}=\frac{\frac1{\sin A}}{\frac1{\sin A}-\sin A}=\frac{1}{1-\sin^2A}=\frac1{\cos^2A}=\sec^2A=\text{LHS}$$

questions.question: Given $f(x)=x-2$ and $g(x)=(x+2)(x^2-4)$, find all points of intersection between $f(x)$ and $g(x)$.
questions.answer:
Since $x^2-4=(x+2)(x-2)$, $g(x)=(x+2)^2(x-2)$. Setting $f(x)=g(x)$:
$$x-2=(x+2)^2(x-2)\Rightarrow(x-2)\left[(x+2)^2-1\right]=0$$
$x=2$, or $(x+2)^2=1\Rightarrow x+2=\pm1\Rightarrow x=-1$ or $x=-3$.
The points of intersection are $(2,0)$, $(-1,-3)$ and $(-3,-5)$.

questions.question: (Functions $f(x)=x-2$ and $g(x)=(x+2)(x^2-4)$.) Sketch the graphs of $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ on the same axes, showing all important features. (Do not find any stationary points.)
questions.answer:
- $f(x)=x-2$ is a straight line with intercepts $(2,0)$ and $(0,-2)$.
- $g(x)=(x+2)^2(x-2)$ is a cubic with a double root at $x=-2$ (it touches the $x$-axis and turns there), a single root at $x=2$, $y$-intercept $(0,-8)$, and positive leading coefficient (falls to $-\infty$ on the left, rises to $+\infty$ on the right).
- They intersect at $(-3,-5)$, $(-1,-3)$ and $(2,0)$ (see graph).

questions.question: (Functions $f(x)=x-2$ and $g(x)=(x+2)(x^2-4)$.) Hence, or otherwise, solve the inequality $x-2<(x+2)(x^2-4)$.
questions.answer:
The inequality holds where the graph of $g$ is above the line $f$: between the first two intersection points and to the right of the last one:
$$-3<x<-1\quad\text{or}\quad x>2.$$

questions.question: A company produces resistors with resistance being normally distributed ($\mu=50\ \Omega$, $\sigma=2\ \Omega$). Resistors below $48\ \Omega$ or exceeding $52\ \Omega$ are defective. Find the percentage of defective resistors.
questions.answer: $48$ and $52$ are one standard deviation below and above the mean. By the empirical rule, about $68\%$ lie within one standard deviation, so $100\%-68\%=32\%$ are defective.

questions.question: (Resistance normally distributed with $\mu=50\ \Omega$, $\sigma=2\ \Omega$; $32\%$ defective.) In a batch of $1000$ resistors, how many are expected to be non-defective?
questions.answer: $1000\times(1-0.32)=680$ resistors.

questions.question: Show that $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(e^x\tan x\right)=e^x\left(\tan^2x+\tan x+1\right)$.
questions.answer:
Product rule with $u=e^x$, $v=\tan x$ ($u'=e^x$, $v'=\sec^2x$):
$$\frac{d}{dx}(e^x\tan x)=e^x\sec^2x+e^x\tan x=e^x(\sec^2x+\tan x)=e^x(\tan^2x+1+\tan x)$$
using $\sec^2x=\tan^2x+1$.

questions.question: Hence evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/3}e^x\left(\tan^2x+\tan x+1\right)dx$.
questions.answer:
By part (a), $e^x\tan x$ is a primitive of the integrand:
$$\int_0^{\pi/3}e^x(\tan^2x+\tan x+1)dx=\Big[e^x\tan x\Big]_0^{\pi/3}=e^{\pi/3}\tan\frac\pi3-e^0\tan0=\sqrt3\,e^{\pi/3}$$

questions.question: The figure below shows the graph of a curve with equation $y=f(x)$. The curve meets the $x$-axis at $(-3,0)$ and the $y$-axis at $(0,2)$. Its maximum point is at $(3,4)$ and a minimum at $(-3,0)$. The line $y=2$ is a horizontal asymptote to the curve. What is the range of $\tfrac12f(x)$?
questions.answer: The range of $f(x)$ is $[0,4]$ (from the minimum $0$ to the maximum $4$). A vertical dilation by $\tfrac12$ halves every $y$-value, so the range of $\tfrac12f(x)$ is $[0,2]$.

questions.question: (Curve $y=f(x)$ as in part (a): $x$-intercept and minimum $(-3,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,2)$, maximum $(3,4)$, horizontal asymptote $y=2$.) Sketch the graph of $g(x)=f(3x)-4$, labelling all key points and asymptotes.
Events $A$ and $B$ are such that $P(A)=\dfrac{3k}4$, $P(B)=k$ and $P(\overline A\cap B)=k^2$ where $0<k<1$. Find the expression for $P(A\cap B)$ in terms of $k$.
questions.answer:
$B$ is split into the part inside $A$ and the part outside $A$: $P(B)=P(A\cap B)+P(\overline A\cap B)$, so
$$P(A\cap B)=k-k^2.$$

questions.question: (Events $A$, $B$ with $P(A)=\tfrac{3k}4$, $P(B)=k$, $P(\overline A\cap B)=k^2$, $0<k<1$, so $P(A\cap B)=k-k^2$.) Given that the two events are independent, find the value of $k$.
questions.answer:
For independent events $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$:
$$k-k^2=\frac{3k}4\cdot k\Rightarrow1-k=\frac{3k}4\ (k\ne0)\Rightarrow4-4k=3k\Rightarrow k=\frac47$$
(The other root of $k(7k-4)=0$ is $k=0$, which is rejected since $0<k<1$.)

questions.question:
The amount of time for Opstra Telecom to respond to a customer query follows the probability density function
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{k}{(5x-1)^2}&x\ge1\\0&0<x<1\end{cases}$$
where $x$ is time in hours. Show that $k=20$.
questions.answer:
The total area under a PDF is $1$:
$$\int_1^\infty\frac k{(5x-1)^2}dx=k\left[-\frac1{5(5x-1)}\right]_1^\infty=k\left(0+\frac1{5(4)}\right)=\frac k{20}=1\Rightarrow k=20.$$

questions.question: (PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{20}{(5x-1)^2}$ for $x\ge1$, and $0$ for $0<x<1$; $x$ in hours.) Calculate the median response time.
questions.answer:
Let the median be $m$, so $\displaystyle\int_1^m\frac{20}{(5x-1)^2}dx=\frac12$:
$$20\left[-\frac1{5(5x-1)}\right]_1^m=4\left(\frac14-\frac1{5m-1}\right)=1-\frac4{5m-1}=\frac12\Rightarrow5m-1=8\Rightarrow m=\frac95=1.8\ \text{hours}.$$

questions.question: (PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{20}{(5x-1)^2}$ for $x\ge1$, and $0$ for $0<x<1$; $x$ in hours.) What is the probability that the company spends more than $2$ hours but less than $3$ hours to respond to the customer query?

The velocity of a particle is given by $\dot x(t)=8t^3e^{t^4}$, where $\dot x(t)$ is velocity in metres per second and $t$ is time in seconds. Initially, the particle is at the origin. Determine the time(s) the particle is at rest.
questions.answer: The particle is at rest when $\dot x=0$: $8t^3e^{t^4}=0$. Since $e^{t^4}>0$ for all $t$, this requires $t=0$. The particle is at rest only at $t=0$ (initially).

questions.question: (Velocity $\dot x(t)=8t^3e^{t^4}$ m/s; initially the particle is at the origin.) Show that the displacement function is $x(t)=2e^{t^4}-2$.
questions.answer:
$$x(t)=\int8t^3e^{t^4}dt=2\int4t^3e^{t^4}dt=2e^{t^4}+C$$
Initially $x(0)=0$: $2e^0+C=0\Rightarrow C=-2$. Hence $x(t)=2e^{t^4}-2$.

questions.question: (Displacement $x(t)=2e^{t^4}-2$ metres.) At what time does the particle reach a displacement of $100$ metres? Give your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.answer: $$2e^{t^4}-2=100\Rightarrow e^{t^4}=51\Rightarrow t^4=\ln51\Rightarrow t=(\ln51)^{1/4}\approx1.41\ \text{seconds}$$

questions.question:
The mass of oranges at Fruit King farm is normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. It is known that $25.78\%$ of these oranges have mass more than $190$ g and $34.46\%$ of them have mass more than $180$ g. Using the table of $z$-scores below, find the mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

| $z$ | 0.35 | 0.4 | 0.45 | 0.5 | 0.55 | 0.6 | 0.65 | 0.7 | 0.75 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.6368 | 0.6554 | 0.6736 | 0.6915 | 0.7088 | 0.7257 | 0.7422 | 0.7580 | 0.7734 |

(The table gives $P(Z<z)$.)
questions.answer:
$P(X<190)=1-0.2578=0.7422$, which the table gives as $z=0.65$:
$$\frac{190-\mu}{\sigma}=0.65\quad(1)$$
$P(X<180)=1-0.3446=0.6554$, which gives $z=0.4$:
$$\frac{180-\mu}{\sigma}=0.4\quad(2)$$
Subtracting (2) from (1): $\dfrac{10}\sigma=0.25\Rightarrow\sigma=40$. Then $180-\mu=0.4(40)=16\Rightarrow\mu=164$.

The mean is $164$ g and the standard deviation is $40$ g.

questions.question: (Orange masses are normally distributed with $\mu=164$ g and $\sigma=40$ g; $P(Z<0.75)=0.7734$ and $P(X<180)=0.6554$.) Two oranges from Fruit King farm are chosen at random. Given that the mass of both oranges is greater than $180$ grams, what is the probability that both of them have a mass less than $194$ g? Give your answer as a percentage to $2$ decimal places.

As shown in the diagram, a sequence of squares is inscribed within a right-angled triangle $ABC$, where $AB=a$, $BC=2a$ and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$. The squares are arranged such that each square touches the hypotenuse $AC$, and the side length is labelled as $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$. By considering similar triangles, show that $a_1=\dfrac23a$.
questions.answer:
The small triangle above the first square (with vertical side $a-a_1$ and horizontal side $a_1$) is similar to triangle $ABC$ (vertical side $a$, horizontal side $2a$). So
$$\frac{a-a_1}{a_1}=\frac{a}{2a}=\frac12\Rightarrow2a-2a_1=a_1\Rightarrow a_1=\frac23a.$$

questions.question: (Squares of side $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ inscribed in right-angled triangle $ABC$ with $AB=a$, $BC=2a$, as in part (a), with $a_1=\tfrac23a$.) Show that the areas of the squares form a geometric sequence. State the common ratio.
questions.answer:
The remaining triangle above each square is similar to the one before it with the same ratio, so each square is $\tfrac23$ the side of the previous one: $a_2=\tfrac23a_1$, $a_3=\tfrac23a_2,\ldots$ (the same argument as in part (a) applies to each smaller triangle).
Areas: $A_1=a_1^2=\tfrac49a^2$, $A_2=a_2^2=\left(\tfrac23a_1\right)^2=\tfrac49A_1$, $A_3=\tfrac49A_2,\ldots$ Each area is $\tfrac49$ of the one before, so the areas form a geometric sequence with common ratio $r=\dfrac49$.

questions.question: (The areas of the squares form a geometric sequence with first term $A_1=\tfrac49a^2$ and common ratio $\tfrac49$.) Find, in terms of $a$, the total sum of the areas of all the squares.
questions.answer:
Since $|r|=\tfrac49<1$ the series converges:
$$S_\infty=\frac{A_1}{1-r}=\frac{\frac49a^2}{1-\frac49}=\frac{\frac49a^2}{\frac59}=\frac45a^2$$

questions.question: Let $f(x)=(x+1)e^x$. Show that $f''(x)=(x+3)e^x$.
questions.answer: Product rule: $f'(x)=e^x+(x+1)e^x=(x+2)e^x$. Again: $f''(x)=e^x+(x+2)e^x=(x+3)e^x$.

questions.question: (Function $f(x)=(x+1)e^x$, with $f'(x)=(x+2)e^x$ and $f''(x)=(x+3)e^x$.) Find any stationary points of $f(x)$, determine their nature, and find any points of inflection.
questions.answer:
**Stationary points:** $f'(x)=0\Rightarrow(x+2)e^x=0\Rightarrow x=-2$ (as $e^x>0$). $f(-2)=-e^{-2}$. Since $f''(-2)=e^{-2}>0$, the point $(-2,-e^{-2})$ is a local minimum.

**Inflection:** $f''(x)=0\Rightarrow x=-3$. $f''$ changes sign there ($f''<0$ for $x<-3$ and $f''>0$ for $x>-3$), so there is a point of inflection at $(-3,-2e^{-3})$.

questions.question: (Function $f(x)=(x+1)e^x$.) Sketch the curve $f(x)$, labelling any stationary points, points of inflection and intercepts with the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis.
questions.answer: Key features: $y$-intercept $(0,1)$; $x$-intercept $(-1,0)$; local minimum $(-2,-e^{-2})$; point of inflection $(-3,-2e^{-3})$; as $x\to-\infty$, $f(x)\to0^-$ (the $x$-axis is a horizontal asymptote); as $x\to\infty$, $f(x)\to\infty$ (see graph).

questions.question: Consider the two curves $L_1$: $y=-x^2+1$ for $0\le x\le1$ and $L_2$: $y=ax^2$ for $x\ge0$. The diagram below shows the area enclosed by these two curves and the $x$- and $y$-axes. Show that the two curves intersect at the point $\left(\sqrt{\dfrac1{1+a}},\dfrac a{1+a}\right)$.
questions.answer: Equating the curves: $-x^2+1=ax^2\Rightarrow(1+a)x^2=1\Rightarrow x^2=\dfrac1{1+a}$. Since $x\ge0$, $x=\sqrt{\dfrac1{1+a}}$. Then $y=ax^2=\dfrac a{1+a}$.

questions.question: (Curves $L_1$: $y=1-x^2$ and $L_2$: $y=ax^2$ ($a>0$), meeting at $x=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1+a}}$. $S_1$ is the region between the two curves, to the left of the intersection; $S_2$ is the region below both curves.) Find the value of $a$ such that the areas of the two regions are equal.
questions.answer:
The total area under $L_1$ from $0$ to $1$ is $\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x^2)dx=\tfrac23$. If $S_1=S_2$ then each is $\tfrac13$.

Let $c=\dfrac1{\sqrt{1+a}}$. Then
$$S_1=\int_0^c\left(1-x^2-ax^2\right)dx=\int_0^c\left(1-(1+a)x^2\right)dx=c-\frac{(1+a)c^3}3=c-\frac c3=\frac{2c}3$$
(using $(1+a)c^2=1$). Setting $S_1=\tfrac13$: $\dfrac{2c}3=\dfrac13\Rightarrow c=\dfrac12\Rightarrow\sqrt{1+a}=2\Rightarrow a=3$.

(The school's three methods all lead to $(1+a)^2(a-3)=0$; $a=-1$ is rejected as $a>0$.)

questions.question: The diagram shows four scenic points located at the vertices of the trapezium $ABCD$. It is given that $AD=BC$, the distance between points $A$ and $B$ is $4$ kilometres, the distance between points $C$ and $D$ is $2$ km, and $\angle DAB=\angle CBA=60^\circ$. A new lookout point, $P$, is to be constructed on segment $CD$ (excluding endpoints), with direct walking tracks built from $P$ to $A$ and from $P$ to $C$. The construction cost is $\$100\,000$ per km for track $AP$ and $\$80\,000$ per km for track $PC$. Let $\angle BAP=\theta$. Show that $AP=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\sin\theta}$.
questions.answer: Drop perpendiculars from $D$ and $C$ to $AB$, meeting it at $E$ and $F$. The trapezium is isosceles, so $AE=BF=\dfrac{4-2}2=1$ km. In $\triangle ADE$: $\tan60^\circ=\dfrac h1\Rightarrow h=\sqrt3$ km (the height of the trapezium). Drop a perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ (meeting it at $H$); $PH=h=\sqrt3$. In $\triangle APH$: $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{AP}\Rightarrow AP=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\sin\theta}$.

questions.question: (Trapezium $ABCD$: $AB=4$ km, $CD=2$ km, $AD=BC$, base angles $60^\circ$, height $\sqrt3$ km; $P$ on $CD$ with $\angle BAP=\theta$.) Find a similar expression for $DP$ in terms of $\theta$.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle APH$: $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{AH}\Rightarrow AH=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\tan\theta}$. Since $DP=EH=AH-AE$,
$$DP=\frac{\sqrt3}{\tan\theta}-1.$$

questions.question: (Trapezium $ABCD$ with $AP=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\sin\theta}$ km and $DP=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\tan\theta}-1$ km; $CD=2$ km; track $AP$ costs $\$100\,000$ per km and track $PC$ costs $\$80\,000$ per km.) Find the value of $\cos\theta$ that minimises the total cost of constructing the two tracks.
questions.answer:
$PC=CD-DP=2-\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\tan\theta}-1\right)=3-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{\tan\theta}$. The total cost is
$$C=100\,000\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{\sin\theta}+80\,000\left(3-\frac{\sqrt3\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\right)$$
$$\frac{dC}{d\theta}=\frac{-100\,000\sqrt3\cos\theta}{\sin^2\theta}+\frac{80\,000\sqrt3}{\sin^2\theta}=\frac{\sqrt3\,(80\,000-100\,000\cos\theta)}{\sin^2\theta}$$
(using $\dfrac{d}{d\theta}\cot\theta=-\operatorname{cosec}^2\theta$). Setting $\dfrac{dC}{d\theta}=0$: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{80\,000}{100\,000}=\dfrac45$ ($\theta\approx36.9^\circ$, which lies between $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ as required for $P$ to be on $CD$).

For $\theta<36.9^\circ$, $\dfrac{dC}{d\theta}<0$ and for $\theta>36.9^\circ$, $\dfrac{dC}{d\theta}>0$ (since $\cos\theta$ decreases as $\theta$ increases), so this is a minimum. The cost is minimised when $\cos\theta=\dfrac45$.
